narrator.name: Affine (SN120)
narrator.role: Subnet team; Jacob Steeves (Const), CEO of Affine and Bittensor co-founder, speaks for it
narrator.one_line: Reinforcement-learning subnet founded in mid 2025 and run as a king-of-the-hill competition where miners upload model checkpoints and the reigning champion takes the emission; led by Bittensor co-founder Jacob Steeves after he left the Opentensor Foundation, so its language is the closest any subnet gets to the founder's own.

statements.quote: Affine is building an incentivized RL environment that pays miners for incremental improvements on tasks like program synthesis and coding.
statements.context: Opening line of the About Affine section in the team's own job postings on web3.career (community moderator and research engineer roles), dated by the site as posted about a year before September 2026.

source.title: Web3 Subnet Community Moderator & Developer Relations at Affine.io

statements.quote: Operating on Bittensor's Subnet 120, we've created a sybil-proof, decoy-proof, copy-proof, and overfitting-proof mechanism that rewards genuine model improvements.
statements.context: Second sentence of the About Affine section in the team's job postings; the same wording appears in the research engineer posting.

source.title: Web3 Subnet Community Moderator & Developer Relations at Affine.io

statements.quote: Our vision is to commoditize reasoning—the highest form of intelligence—by directing and aggregating the work of a large, non-permissioned group on RL tasks to break the intelligence sound barrier.
statements.context: Vision sentence in the team's job postings; the phrase commoditize reasoning is repeated by third parties as the subnet's tagline and by Jacob Steeves's 2026 conference bios.

source.title: Web3 Research Engineer, ML / RL / Agents at Affine.io

statements.quote: Affine's strength comes from its open, global network of miners, validators, and contributors competing to advance RL.
statements.context: From the community moderator posting, describing who the role would serve.

source.title: Web3 Subnet Community Moderator & Developer Relations at Affine.io

statements.quote: Success means a thriving, self-sustaining community where contributors are empowered to participate, compete, and innovate.
statements.context: Closing line of the community moderator posting, describing what the team counts as success.

source.title: Web3 Subnet Community Moderator & Developer Relations at Affine.io

statements.quote: A direct market for engineers to upload open models that advance the frontier on RL tasks – and get paid for it, secured by the Bittensor blockchain and instant crypto payouts.
statements.context: Wording reproduced on the Subnet Alpha profile of Affine as the project's own pitch; the primary (an earlier README or site copy) was not reachable, so attribution rests on the aggregator.

statements.quote: One of the largest subnets on Bittensor, Affine, was built by Chinese developers and is becoming one of the most competitive mechanisms on the network.
statements.context: Jacob Steeves, Affine CEO and Bittensor co-founder, answering ChainCatcher's question about how engineers are distributed across the roughly 128 subnets; interview published in Chinese and read in Bitget's English translation.

source.title: Interview with Bittensor Founder Jacob: Applying Mining to AI, Top 3 Subnets Built by Chinese Teams

statements.quote: Once Chinese miners enter a subnet, competition immediately becomes much fiercer, to the point that many of the original participants choose to exit.
statements.context: Jacob Steeves in the same ChainCatcher interview, asked what message he brought to Asian developers and investors.

source.title: Interview with Bittensor Founder Jacob: Applying Mining to AI, Top 3 Subnets Built by Chinese Teams

statements.quote: about 128 subnets, each collaborating and competing around different tasks such as inference, training, reinforcement learning, code agents, storage, prediction/trading signals
statements.context: Jacob Steeves describing the network as a whole in the ChainCatcher interview, before naming Affine, Ridges and Lium as examples.

source.title: Interview with Bittensor Founder Jacob: Applying Mining to AI, Top 3 Subnets Built by Chinese Teams

statements.quote: …launching a subnet and compete, good supply is amplified by incentives, poor supply is naturally eliminated
statements.context: Jacob Steeves on how subnets sort their miners, in the ChainCatcher interview; the translation renders the clause as a fragment.

source.title: Interview with Bittensor Founder Jacob: Applying Mining to AI, Top 3 Subnets Built by Chinese Teams

statements.quote: Jacob Robert Steeves is the co-founder of Bittensor, an open-source protocol supporting a decentralized machine-learning network built on blockchain technology.
statements.context: Speaker bio for Jacob Steeves, listed as CEO of Affine, on the Paris Blockchain Week 2026 site (event 15 to 16 April 2026); conference bios are normally supplied by the speaker.

source.title: Jacob Robert Steeves - Bittensor, speaker page

statements.quote: Affine is a Bittensor subnet (netuid 120) that crowns miners by a single teacher-anchored distillation score — Reason (Λ2), not an LLM judge.
statements.context: First sentence of AGENTS.md in the AffineFoundation/affine repository, the team's public command-center document, status-dated 10 September 2026; markdown emphasis removed.

statements.quote: We want a score that stays benchmark-isomorphic under adversarial pressure on the capability axis.
statements.context: AGENTS.md stating the design goal, in a document that also records that the Reason score's correlation with coding ability inverts on the live SN120 board; markdown emphasis removed.

statements.quote: King-of-the-hill subnet. Miners upload checkpoints privately to a validator-controlled bucket … The validator crowns the reigning king by a single teacher-anchored distillation score … Replayability is the trust model: two checkpoints + public D + affine/score.py → recompute the verdict
statements.context: The llms.txt operating rules on affine.io, which carry rule changes dated 2 to 14 September 2026; three lines joined with ellipses.

statements.quote: His work explores incentive-based computer networks and open systems for producing and coordinating machine intelligence.
statements.context: Speaker bio for Jacob Steeves, listed as CEO of Affine, on the Exploit Summit 2026 site (event 28 to 29 September 2026), read on 15 September 2026.

statements.quote: a crown is paid for at most 72 hours after it is won. Every crown inside its window gets one equal share (2 paid crowns = 50/50, 3 = thirds); an older crown earns nothing even while it still holds the throne for duels; no paid crown = the emission burns.
statements.context: The Payout rule block on the affine.io homepage, dated 2026-09-14.

metaphors.label: commodity
metaphors.wording: commoditize reasoning—the highest form of intelligence
metaphors.lineage_notes: Extends Jacob Steeves's long-running frame of Bittensor as a market for digital commodities; see the VirtualBacon interview summary at https://x.com/virtualbacon/status/2037312527143510415 (subnets create markets for digital commodities like gradients).

metaphors.label: market
metaphors.wording: A direct market for engineers to upload open models
metaphors.lineage_notes: Foundation and founder language; also in Steeves's description of Lium as a permissionless market in the same ChainCatcher interview.

metaphors.label: king of the hill
metaphors.lineage_notes: Crown, king, throne, reign, duel and dethrone run through the 2026 rules and code; winner-take-all framing is shared with Minos SN107 (see sn107-004).

metaphors.label: competition
metaphors.wording: one of the most competitive mechanisms on the network
metaphors.lineage_notes: Common to most subnet teams; Steeves ties it to Chinese miners entering.

foundation.mission.summary: Pay miners for incremental improvements on reinforcement-learning tasks such as program synthesis and coding, inside a mechanism built to resist sybils, decoys, copying and overfitting.

foundation.vision.summary: Commoditize reasoning by aggregating the work of a large, non-permissioned group on RL tasks until the intelligence sound barrier breaks.

foundation.values.summary: A score that stays honest under adversarial pressure, with every verdict replayable and every crowned model published.

audience.summary: Miners, validators and contributors described as an open, global network competing to advance RL; Steeves singles out Chinese miners as the force that makes subnets fiercer.

positioning.category.summary: For the subnet: an incentivized RL environment, a direct market for engineers, and since 2026 a king-of-the-hill competition. For the network: an open-source protocol for a decentralised machine-learning network, in which subnets collaborate and compete around tasks.

positioning.differentiator.summary: A mechanism claimed to be sybil-proof, decoy-proof, copy-proof and overfitting-proof, and by 2026 a teacher-anchored distillation score rather than an LLM judge.

positioning.reason.summary: An open global network of competitors, and the claim that Affine is among the largest and most competitive mechanisms on Bittensor; the network filters supply by incentive.

value.functional.summary: Engineers upload open models and get paid, with crown emission paid for at most 72 hours and burned when no crown qualifies.

value.self_expressive.summary: Contributors are cast as empowered participants who compete and innovate.

messaging.proof.summary: Anti-gaming properties, size and competitiveness on the network, and replayable verdicts.

voice.summary: Terse engineering rules written for miners (crowns, windows, burns), and a founder who talks about competition getting fiercer.

relationship.summary: The subnet's CEO is Bittensor's co-founder and presents himself as such in every bio; the subnet is his only subnet and his return to building.

language.term.summary: Commoditize reasoning; king, crown, throne, reign, dethrone, duel; teacher-anchored distillation score; Reason and Grounding.

subnet.self.summary: An incentivized RL environment that became a king-of-the-hill distillation contest: private checkpoint uploads, a frozen teacher, one crowned king, a 72-hour paid window, and published, replayable verdicts.

subnet.network.summary: Bittensor is described in the founder's own vocabulary: an open-source protocol for a decentralised machine-learning network, incentive-based computer networks, about 128 subnets collaborating and competing, where incentives amplify good supply and eliminate poor supply.

words_avoided: community in the marketing sense on the 2026 site

coinages.meaning: Treat reasoning as a commodity produced by an open, non-permissioned group and priced by the mechanism.
A threshold of machine reasoning the team says aggregated RL work will break through.
A single reigning model holds the emission until a challenger beats it by a statistical margin.
Scoring miners by likelihood under a frozen teacher model rather than by an LLM judge.

genealogy.summary: In 2025 Affine described itself as an incentivized RL environment with a mechanism proofed against sybils, decoys, copying and overfitting, and gave its vision as commoditizing reasoning to break the intelligence sound barrier [sn120-001] [sn120-002] [sn120-003]. Steeves, speaking for it in late 2025, framed Bittensor as subnets collaborating and competing where incentives amplify good supply, and pointed to Chinese miners as the source of Affine's competitiveness [sn120-009] [sn120-010] [sn120-007].

By September 2026 the public voice is the rulebook: a king-of-the-hill subnet scored by a frozen teacher, crowns paid for 72 hours, emission burned when no crown qualifies, every verdict replayable [sn120-012] [sn120-014] [sn120-016]. The vision sentence survives only in conference bios that describe incentive-based computer networks and open systems for coordinating machine intelligence [sn120-015].
genealogy.shift: From a vision statement about commoditizing reasoning to a mechanism-first register of kings, crowns and burns; the team's own AGENTS.md concedes the score measures distillation fidelity under adversarial pressure rather than raw capability.

relations.note: The subnet's vocabulary (commodity, market, incentive-based networks) is the founder's own, since he runs it.
Steeves names Ridges as a large coding-agent subnet optimized collectively by miners in the same interview.
Both Affine and Minos run winner-take-all mechanisms; Minos calls it Winner-Take-All, Affine calls it a crown.
